name: Deep sequence models (LSTM) for daily return direction

origin.source_title: Deep learning with long short-term memory networks for financial market predictions (FAU DP 11/2017; European Journal of Operational Research 2018)

how_it_works.simple: A neural network with memory reads the last 240 days of returns for each stock and guesses whether it will beat the others tomorrow.
how_it_works.analogy: Like a coach who watches each player's last season of games to guess who will score in the next match.
how_it_works.precise: Train an LSTM on sequences of 240 standardized daily returns for S&P 500 constituents to classify whether next-day return exceeds the cross-sectional median; go long the top k and short the bottom k each day. Gains are partly explained by a short-term reversal pattern in volatile stocks.

rule: Each day, rank S&P 500 constituents by the LSTM's predicted probability of beating the median tomorrow; buy the top 10 and short the bottom 10 equally weighted at the close and hold one day; retrain every 250 trading days on the prior 750 days.
data_needed: Daily total returns of index constituents with historical membership lists
Transaction cost assumption (5 bps per half-turn in the paper)
economic_rationale: Nonlinear models can pick up short-term reversal and volatility patterns that linear models miss (Fischer and Krauss).
why_it_might_fail: The paper itself shows the edge deteriorating after 2010, with the LSTM roughly flat after costs over 2010-2015. Daily long-short on 20 stocks has high turnover, and a pre-cost Sharpe of 5.8 is typical of short-term reversal signals that do not survive realistic costs.

reported_results.notes: After 5 bps per half-turn. Before costs: Sharpe 5.83, 0.46 percent per day. Random forest after costs Sharpe 1.87. The authors note 2010-2015 as a period of deterioration where the LSTM only kept capital about constant after costs.

post_publication_evidence: Within the paper's own sample, returns faded after 2010. Later Kaggle competitions (Jane Street Market Prediction 2021, Real-Time Market Data Forecasting 2024-25) used GRU/LSTM and tree ensembles, but their scores and live results were not verified for this entry.

implementations.notes: Has LSTM, GRU and transformer baselines with standard datasets.

relevance.reason: Shows how strong deep-learning backtests decay; for a handful of currencies there is too little data to train such models well.
